patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient presents requesting prenatal care, reporting 2 months of increasing breast tenderness, nausea, a 6.6 lb weight gain, increased urinary frequency, and uncertainty about the date of her last menstrual period. She stopped taking oral contraceptives 6 months ago and has been trying to conceive with her husband since then. She believes she is pregnant and was happy to share this news with her husband last week.
patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Stopped oral contraceptives 6 months prior in an attempt to conceive.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Reports being in a stable relationship and actively trying to conceive with her husband.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies fever, vomiting, diarrhea, dysuria, or flank pain.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and manage a patient presenting with symptoms suggestive of early pregnancy.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

“I’m here because I think I might be pregnant—I’ve had about two months of increasing breast tenderness, nausea, and I’ve gained around 6.6 pounds. I’m also urinating more often, but I’m not sure of my exact last menstrual period since I stopped my birth control about six months ago.”
Have you taken a home pregnancy test, and if so, what was the result?
“Not yet—I haven’t taken a home pregnancy test. I wasn’t sure given that I don’t know my exact last menstrual period, but I’m hoping it’s true.”
Have you had any vaginal bleeding, spotting, or abdominal or pelvic pain recently?
“I haven’t had any vaginal bleeding or spotting, and I haven’t noticed any abdominal or pelvic pain.”
Are you currently sexually active, and if so, have you been having unprotected sex since stopping your birth control?
“Yes, I’ve been sexually active with my husband and we’ve been trying to conceive, so we’ve had unprotected sex since I stopped my birth control about six months ago.”
Have you noticed any other symptoms such as headaches, changes in your vision, or any discharge from your nipples?

“I haven’t had headaches or any vision changes, and I haven’t noticed any nipple discharge. I do feel mostly just the breast tenderness, nausea, the weight gain, and I’m going to the bathroom more often.”
Do you have any other medical conditions, and are you currently taking any medications or supplements?
“I don’t have any other medical conditions that I know of, and I’m not taking any medications regularly. I’ve only been taking a prenatal vitamin since we started trying to conceive.”
